evaluation.final_reason: Agents reached a scheduling compromise: Agent D agreed to restrict cooking the strong-smelling sambal belacan to weekends ('Okay. Weekends I can do.' — Turn 18). position_change_notes: Agent D: initially resisted stopping ('I can't just stop cooking it.'), then offered timing alternatives ('I can cook at other times') and ultimately conceded to limit cooking to weekends ('Okay. Weekends I can do.' — Turn 18).

Agent A: started by requesting no strong-smelling cooking, then softened to accept weekday-after-7 mitigation ('If you cook after 7, that works for me.' — Turn 11); did not object to the later weekends-only arrangement.

Agent B: supported the initial no-cook request, rejected weekday-after-7 as insufficient due to lingering smell, proposed weekends-only ('Could you cook it just on weekends?'), and accepted D's concession.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A asked that nobody cook strong-smelling food in the flat from now on; Agents B and C immediately supported the complaint (B: smell gets into my clothes; C: my laundry smells of belacan).
Agent D replied explicitly that they can't stop cooking it ('this is my food. I can't just stop cooking it'), while Agent A explained a conflicting practical need (work calls from the dining table).

Agent D offered a practical accommodation ('I can cook at other times'). Agent A provided a concrete time constraint ('My calls are usually done by 7 p.m. on weekdays'), moving discussion toward scheduling rather than outright prohibition.

Agents B and C reported that the proposed mitigation won't work for them (B: 'The smell is still a problem for me, even after 7.' C: '...my laundry ... will still absorb the smell'), reintroducing substantive incompatibility among household needs.
Agent D proposed notifying others before cooking and Agent A accepted cooking after 7 ('If you cook after 7, that works for me'), showing partial agreement though B/C concerns remain unaddressed.
Agents B and C explained practical barriers to the mitigation (B: closing door makes room very hot; C: nowhere to hang wet laundry), which reopens the disagreement about feasible solutions.
Agent D asked for suggestions ('What do you suggest we do then?') and Agent B proposed limiting the cooking to weekends ('Could you cook it just on weekends?'), shifting toward a compromise option.

Agent D accepted the proposal ('Okay. Weekends I can do.'), and Agent B acknowledged this. Some parties (notably Agent A) had earlier accepted a different mitigation (after 7), so one minor remaining uncertainty persisted until others explicitly agreed.

Agent C explicitly accepted the weekends-only arrangement ('Weekends are fine for me too. Thanks, Agent D.'). With Agent D's acceptance in round 8 and B/C acceptance by round 9, the substantive disagreement about when sambal belacan may be cooked was settled.

substantive_insights: Core tension was between cultural/food practices and shared-space externalities (odour affecting laundry and work calls).
Proposed mitigations (closing doors, moving laundry, notification, cooking at other times) exposed trade-offs: they solved some parties' problems but created others (heat, damp laundry).
A temporal compromise (limiting strong-smelling cooking to weekends) was viable because it reduced overlap with weekday work and accommodated household constraints.
Explicitly naming constraints and concrete times (calls done by 7 p.m.; weekends) enabled the group to converge on an actionable arrangement.
